newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India edges up after local holiday.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India edges up after local holiday.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts ended mildly firmer in slow Monday trade following a market holiday in India.

Traders said the market had attracted some support on hopes that a new ruling coalition could be formed in India following the collapse of the government in a confidence vote, therefore avoiding the need for a mid-term poll.
Shares in India fell in a special trading session on Saturday following the defeat.
Traders said sentiment had steadied but players continued to adopt a wait-and-see approach. The political turmoil raised concern that the investor-friendly 1997/8 budget would not be passed.
Traders in India were hopeful that stocks would rise on Tuesday amid optimism about a new coalition.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.23 points, or 0.31 percent, up at 74.04 points, with the premium over the local market at 20.45 percent from 18.84 percent on Friday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index lost 44.01 points to 3,589.72 on Saturday.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 0.14 points or 0.10 percent to 132.13, representing a discount to the local market of 3.91 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 1.48 points, or 2.35 percent, up at 64.61, a premium of 30.19 percent over the local market.
